Cc: sre@acmepayments.com
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Spike in p99 on Hosted API after go-live

Hi Dylan,

We went live with the Redwood Hosted API for our fraud-check flow at 08:30 PT and immediately saw intermittent p99 spikes up to ~12s in the first 10 minutes. P95 looks reasonable (~450ms) but the p99 tail is wreaking havoc on our end-to-end SLA and retry logic.

Attached are sampling logs from our side plus a short flamegraph from our agent. The errors are not 5xx from Redwood — requests eventually succeed — but the user-visible latency causes timeouts in our orchestration. Can the Redwood team help investigate whether this is a cold-start/warmup issue tied to autoscale spin-up? We need a short-term mitigation and a longer-term fix; this is causing paging for our on-call.

Thanks,
Janelle Rivera
Sr. Integration Lead | Acme Payments

Short answer: we are triaging now. My immediate ask for you: can you confirm if the requests showing the tail are hitting the same model variant (gpt-small-16b-rt) and whether they have heavy system prompt/context sizes? That helps us rule in/out KV cache misses vs. cold GPU instance initialization.

I'm looping in Grace (SRE lead for runtime) and Marissa (our Sales escalation lead) to coordinate. We'll aim to get a protective mitigation (short-lived fallback to a lower-latency variant or temporary traffic throttling) within the next 2 hours while we investigate root cause.

Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Spike in p99 on Hosted API after go-live — Investigation summary and mitigation

Hi all — summary from runtime team after correlating logs and traces: 

Findings:
- Correlation with infra metrics shows a pattern of instance attach + model load steps contributing ~7–11s in the p99 tail for the observed timestamps (us-west-2). The autoscaler behavior triggered new GPU instances when concurrency exceeded 120r/s for the model pool.
- The affected requests show large system prompts (avg ~2.2k tokens) causing initial KV allocation and longer kernel selection time on first decode pass; subsequent requests to the same warmed instance show p95/p99 under 600ms.
- We did not find an application-level retry bug on the customer side; delays are server-side initialization.

Immediate mitigations applied (completed 30 min after initial page):
- Enabled short-lived pre-warmed instances in the customer's hosted pool (5 pre-warm slots) to cover peak ramp windows. This reduced observed p99 to ~850ms during subsequent ramp tests.
- Deployed a temporary traffic steering rule to route high-priority traffic to a smaller, lower-latency variant (gpt-small-8b-fast) when instance attach latency is detected.

Longer-term actions (tracked INF-1897):
- Optimize model load path: reduce kernel selection latency by caching selection for known prompt-size distributions (ETA Q4).
- Enhance autoscaler warmup policies: smarter predictive spin-up based on historical ramp patterns and HubSpot schedule signals (ETA Q3 pilot).
- Add per-route pre-warm configuration in Console so customers can opt-in and set expected ramp windows (ETA Q3).

Customer comms suggested (for Dylan/Marissa):
- Short note to Acme acknowledging the root cause (instance init + KV allocation for large prompts), listing mitigations already applied, and commitment to timeline for permanent fixes.
- Offer a one-month credit and optional migration assistance to Dedicated capacity if they want immediate SLA guarantees.

Logs/attachments: uploaded p99-spike-logs-2026-08-28.zip to the Drive link and created INF-1897 in Jira with traces.

Grace O'Connor
SRE Lead, Runtime | Redwood Inference
